marks.gloss_en: שיפועי אהלים כאהלים דמו -- a handbreadth of slope counts as a tent's roof
this was said only where its roof is not a handbreadth wide; if it is, it is forbidden
a grooms' canopy may be spread and may be dismantled
שנאמר ״והפלא ה׳ את מכתך״ -- the 'astonishment' among the curses is the forgetting of Torah (Rav's own derivation)
כשהוא אומר ״לכן הנני יוסף להפליא... הפלא ופלא״ -- הוי אומר הפלאה זו תורה (Rav's own derivation)
the Torah is destined to be forgotten from Israel
שנאמר ״והשלחתי רעב בארץ... לשמוע את דברי ה׳״, וכתיב ״ישוטטו לבקש את דבר ה׳ ולא ימצאו״ (the Sages' own derivation)
the verses: 'I will send a famine in the land ... for hearing the words of the Lord' and 'they will roam to seek the word of the Lord and not find it' (Amos 8:11-12)
יכול יהו כל הכלים מיטמאין... תלמוד לומר ״כל אשר בתוכו יטמא״ ״מכל האוכל״ -- foods, not vessels (the baraita's own derivation)
אמר ליה: לא אמרינן... דתניא: אוכלין מיטמאין באויר כלי חרס ואין כלים מיטמאין -- were the oven as if full of impurity, vessels in it too would be impure
the baraita: foods become impure in the airspace of an earthenware vessel
שנאמר ״כי לא תשכח מפי זרעו״ (RSBY's own derivation)
אלא מה אני מקיים ״ישוטטו לבקש את דבר ה׳ ולא ימצאו״? -- RSBY raises his opponents' verse against his own position
R' Shimon ben Yochai: Heaven forfend that the Torah be forgotten from Israel
והאיתמר: סיאנא אסור -- but it was stated that a felt hat is forbidden! (an amoraic-memra contradiction; no dedicated kind)
Rav Sheshet b. R' Idi: this felt hat is permitted [on Shabbat]
אלא לא קשיא: הא דמיהדק, הא דלא מיהדק -- permitted when fitted firmly, forbidden when not (= p_sayana_chiluk_mihadak; the first answer, the handbreadth, having fallen)
אלא מעתה, שרביב בגלימא טפח הכי נמי דמיחייב? -- if a handbreadth brim made it forbidden, a cloak extended a handbreadth would make one liable; unanswered -- the stam turns to another resolution (אלא)
if so, one who extended his cloak a handbreadth would also be liable [for a tent]

אם טהורה היא ואם טמאה היא בהדיא כתיב ביה -- whether it is impure is written explicitly; no one could fail to know it. Not answered: the stam re-reads (אלא: ראשונה או שניה) -- see header on the explicates gap
it is written explicitly: 'of all food that is eaten [on which water comes shall be impure]' (Lev 11:34)
הא נמי מתניתין היא? כדתנן: השרץ שנמצא בתנור, הפת שבתוכו שניה -- the degree is also taught in a mishna; how would none understand?
the mishna: a sheretz found in an oven -- the bread in it is second-degree, for the oven is first
מסתפקא להו הא דאמר ליה רב אדא בר אהבה לרבא -- they are in doubt over Rav Adda bar Ahava's proposal that the oven be viewed as full of impurity, making the bread first-degree
Rav Adda bar Ahava: let us view this oven as though it were full of impurity
the baraita: a large wineskin may be spread on Shabbat
Abaye: and a canopy, even by ten people, is forbidden
the baraita: a stove one of whose legs fell off may be moved
'the word of the Lord' -- that is halakha
'they will roam to seek': a woman will take a loaf of teruma and go round the synagogues and study halls to know whether it is impure or pure, and none will understand
